```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

As always, the first step was navigating to the proper directory
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
```

My next task was copying the bin files into the genome folder. I needed to build up a fairly expansive list of commands to accomplish this, starting with the following line of code to establish my loop.
```{bash}
while read bin;do echo $bin;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

With this underlying framework set up, I established the paths the files should take to get to the desired folder with the following line.
```{bash}
while read bin;do echo "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa";done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```


Alright! Now that I had the necessary files identified and their paths charted, I finally copied them into the desired folder with this code.
```{bash}
while read bin;do cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

I used good ole' ls to make sure that my copies had made it to genomes.
```{bash}
ls genomes
```

Having made sure everything was where it needed to be, I made a shell script and -following the established nomenclature- saved it as "run_gtdbtk.sh" to the gtdbtk directory. Within this shell I pasted the following code and saved the script.
```{bash}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=120
#SBATCH --ntasks=2 --mem=56gb

echo "Starting gtdbtk in $(pwd) at $(date)"

shopt -s expand_aliases
alias gtdbtk='apptainer run -B /pvol:/pvol,/pvol/data/mg/gtdbtkdata/release207_v2/:/refdata /pvol/data/sif/gtdbtk.sif'

gtdbtk classify_wf -x fa --cpus 2 --genome_dir genomes --out_dir out --skip_ani_screen

echo "Finished gtdbtk in $(pwd) at $(date)"
```

Because my shell script was saved, I was able to submit it at a request to our servers by running this code from the terminal.
```{bash}
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh
#batch job 536
```

To stay updated on its progress, I ran a tail script.
```{bash}
tail -f slurm-536.out
```

Once that job finished, I checked the contents of my output folder with a list command.
```{bash}
ls -l out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

The gitignore file included in the framework I was provided with ensured that git would... ignore - everything in my out folders. I therefore copied my most important output, the tsv file, back up into the gtdbtk directory with this code.
```{bash}
cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```

Taxonomic classification of the most complete bins with GTDB-Tk. Commands for this step were run in `gtdbtk/`.
